evidence: NARROWED: Foreman ownership is defined (SOFTWARE-FACTORY-VISION.md:43,49), so the claim's 'without a defined owner' premise is overbroad. The material gap is a project-work liveness and recovery contract: the factory promises the human need not keep conversations alive and work reaches evidenced outcomes (SOFTWARE-FACTORY-VISION.md:11,29-35), while its task recipes specify ownership/completion criteria but no observation or wake when a delegated worker or the foreman goes silent (71-77). Its recovery brief applies to recurring monitoring on resurrection (77), and scheduling/measurement is explicitly future instance design (131). CURRENT-DESIGN.md:15-17 reconciles graph/Herdr/threads effects; 32-34 defines an approved, specific transcript-summarizer activation path, not general project-work supervision; 9 keeps project tasks in external systems. DESIGN-NOTES.md:132 explicitly leaves surfacing unattended incoming work open; 183-187 excludes project tasks from graph bookkeeping. Concrete failure: a worker accepts a Beads task, stops responding before completion, and no defined observer distinguishes declared waiting from a stall or wakes the foreman/successor; the human must discover/restart it, contrary to the factory promise. This is a factory/work-system design gap, not a demand that graph own a scheduler.
